title: What VAT Actually Does to a KES 1,000,000 Transaction in Kenya (2026 Scenarios)
description: Sixty-second arithmetic for the six most common VAT situations on a KES 1M Kenyan business transaction: standard-rated sale, VAT-inclusive extraction, zero-rated export with input credit, exempt supply cost leakage, and the cost of filing late. Illustrative calculations at the 16% standard rate.
attribution: SmartVAT Kenya (smartvatkenya.co.ke). Illustrative scenarios computed at the 16% standard rate (VAT Act, Cap. 476) and penalty formulas (TPA ss.39-40). Figures are rounded to the nearest shilling. This is general information, not tax advice on a specific matter.

records.scenario: A. Standard-rated sale, VAT exclusive pricing
records.note: The invoice shows KES 1,160,000; you remit KES 160,000 less any input VAT.

records.scenario: B. Standard-rated sale, VAT inclusive pricing
records.note: The KRA 'fraction' method. Your true revenue is KES 862,069 — quoting prices VAT-inclusive changes your margin maths.

records.scenario: C. Zero-rated export with KES 600,000 inputs
records.calculation: Output VAT 0 - input VAT on KES 600,000 (16%)
records.note: Zero-rated ≠ exempt: you can still claim the KES 96,000 input credit and build a refund position (claimable within 12 months).

records.scenario: D. Exempt supply with KES 600,000 inputs
records.calculation: No output VAT; input VAT on KES 600,000 is not claimable
records.note: Exempt status turns KES 96,000 of input VAT into a permanent cost — a 9.6% margin hit on this transaction versus the zero-rated case.

records.scenario: E. Filing scenario B's return 1 month late
records.calculation: Late filing: higher of KES 10,000 or 5% × KES 137,931 = KES 10,000 (minimum applies, per month outstanding); late payment: 5%; interest: 1%/month compounding
records.note: Owing KES 137,931 and being one month late already costs KES 18,276 before the principal.

records.scenario: F. Scenario E left unfiled and unpaid for 12 months
records.calculation: Filing penalty 10,000 × 12 months outstanding + late payment 6,897 + 12 months compounding interest at 1%/month on KES 137,931
records.note: Total cost of KES 282,321 on a KES 137,931 bill: twice the tax itself. The 2026 amnesty or a waiver application exists for exactly this hole.
